title: US 10-year yield nears 5% as hot CPI cements Fed rate-hike bets
content:
The US 10-year Treasury yield climbed to **4.98%** on 11 September 2026, its highest since 2023 and within sight of the psychologically important 5% threshold, after August CPI data reinforced expectations of further Fed tightening. Headline CPI held at 3.4% year-on-year as forecast, but core CPI rose 0.3% month-on-month, above the 0.2% consensus, while producer prices also ran hot.

Money markets raised the odds of a 25bp hike at the Fed's 15-16 September meeting to **88%**, from 71% before the data. The synchronised rise in borrowing costs pressured rate-sensitive equities and added to a broader global bond sell-off already under way.

title: Brent tops $100/bbl as US-Iran tanker war escalates in Hormuz
content:
Brent crude broke above **$100/bbl** on 9 September 2026 for the first time since July, extending a rally fuelled by escalating US-Iran clashes around the Strait of Hormuz. WTI surged as much as 7% to around **$103/bbl**, its highest since May, after US forces struck three Iranian oil tankers on 5 September under a new tanker-for-tanker policy, prompting Iranian strikes on vessels and a missile attack on US warships in the Gulf.

The escalation has stoked fears of disruption to a chokepoint carrying roughly a fifth of global seaborne oil, compounding inflation pressures and adding to bets on further central bank tightening; energy shares rallied while broader risk sentiment weakened.

title: Wall Street posts worst four-day skid since June before Friday bounce
content:
The S&P 500 fell for a fourth straight session on 10 September 2026, its longest losing streak since June, closing at its lowest level since July as the Nasdaq 100 dropped 1.1%; for the week, the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite fell **1.6%**, **0.8%** and 0.7% respectively. Surging oil prices and Treasury yields nearing 5% drove the declines, reviving fears the Fed could resume raising rates.

Sentiment turned on Friday as in-line August CPI and a pullback in oil allowed the S&P 500 to rise **0.29%**, snapping the losing streak, though investors remained cautious ahead of the Fed's 16 September decision.
